title: Derivation of the Tangent Sum Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Derive the standard formula for the tangent of the sum of two angles: \tan(A + B) = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}.

steps.title: Express tan(A + B) as a Quotient of Sine and Cosine
steps.mathExpression: \tan(A + B) = \frac{\sin(A + B)}{\cos(A + B)} = \frac{\sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B}
steps.explanation: Write tan(A + B) = sin(A + B)/cos(A + B) and expand both numerator and denominator using the sine and cosine addition formulas.
steps.why: By definition, tan(theta) = sin(theta)/cos(theta) wherever cos(theta) != 0.

steps.title: Divide Numerator and Denominator by cos A cos B
steps.mathExpression: \tan(A + B) = \frac{\dfrac{\sin A \cos B}{\cos A \cos B} + \dfrac{\cos A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B}}{\dfrac{\cos A \cos B}{\cos A \cos B} - \dfrac{\sin A \sin B}{\cos A \cos B}}
steps.explanation: Assuming cos A != 0 and cos B != 0, divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the product cos A cos B.
steps.why: Dividing numerator and denominator by the same nonzero quantity preserves the value of the fraction.

steps.title: Simplify Each Term to Tangent Ratios
steps.explanation: Cancel common cosine factors and replace sin A / cos A with tan A and sin B / cos B with tan B.
steps.why: Each ratio simplifies directly via the definition of tangent.
